title: Preclinical In Vivo Validation of the RAD51 Test for Identification of Homologous Recombination-Deficient Tumors and Patient Stratification.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: ABL503 bispecific antibody targeting 4-1BB (TNFRSF9) restored the functions of 4-1BB+ exhausted CD8+ TILs which were unresponsive to anti-PD1 blockade, and combination with anti-PD1 enhanced functional restoration in vitro and tumor growth inhibition in vivo.

validated_targets.specific_model_name: Patient-derived HCC and ovarian cancer single-cell suspensions; humanized hPD1/hPDL1/h4-1BB triple-knock-in mice

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Combination of ABL503 and anti-PD1 blockade enhanced functional restoration of exhausted CD8+ TILs beyond that achieved by anti-PD1 blockade alone, with improved tumor growth inhibition in vivo.
validated_targets.specific_model_name: Patient-derived HCC and ovarian cancer single-cell suspensions; humanized hPD1/hPDL1/h4-1BB triple-knock-in mice

evidence_summary: GD2-targeted immunoliposomes (aGD2-SIL(DXR)) inhibited metastatic growth in neuroblastoma models; NGR peptide-targeted liposomes (NGR-SL(DXR)) targeting aminopeptidase N (ANPEP) led to tumor regression, vascular destruction, and prolonged survival in orthotopic neuroblastoma xenografts, with enhanced effects from combined targeting.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Anti-GD2 immunoliposomes loaded with doxorubicin selectively inhibited metastatic growth of human neuroblastoma models.

NGR peptide-targeted liposomes against aminopeptidase N (ANPEP) yielded tumor regression, destruction of tumor vasculature, and prolonged survival in orthotopic neuroblastoma xenografts; antivascular effects also shown in lung and ovarian cancer models.
validated_targets.specific_model_name: orthotopic neuroblastoma xenografts, chick embryo chorioallantoic assay, lung and ovarian cancer models

evidence_summary: Conditional downregulation of ERBB2 in NIH3T3-her2 xenografts by anhydrotetracycline caused rapid tumor regression, decreased Ki-67, and increased apoptosis (caspase-3 and TUNEL); complete remission rates correlated with initial tumor size.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Switching off HER-2/neu expression via anhydrotetracycline in NIH3T3-her2 xenografts led to rapid tumor regression, decreased proliferation (Ki-67) and induction of apoptosis (caspase-3, TUNEL), demonstrating its dependency for tumor maintenance.

title: Switching off HER-2/neu in a tetracycline-controlled mouse tumor model leads to apoptosis and tumor-size-dependent remission.

evidence_summary: Gonadotropin treatment upregulated EGFR expression in IOSE-80PC ovarian surface epithelial cells via ERK1/2 and PI3K signaling pathways, as demonstrated by mRNA and protein assays and inhibitor-based pathway validation.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: FSH and LH treatment increased EGFR mRNA and protein levels in IOSE-80PC cells, and inhibition of PI3K or ERK1/2 partially blocked this upregulation.
FSH and LH increased ERK1/2 kinase activity within 5-10 min; PD98059, an ERK1/2 inhibitor, partially blocked gonadotropin-induced EGFR upregulation.
FSH and LH increased PI3K activity; LY294002, a PI3K inhibitor, partially blocked gonadotropin-induced EGFR upregulation.

title: Gonadotropins upregulate the epidermal growth factor receptor through activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases and phosphatidyl-inositol-3-kinase in human ovarian surface epithelial cells.

evidence_summary: Acquired cisplatin-resistant HX/155cisR cells showed elevated glutathione and metallothionein levels, reduced intracellular drug accumulation, and decreased DNA platination, demonstrating multifocal resistance mechanisms.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: HX/155cisR cells exhibited 1.9-fold resistance to cadmium chloride, indicating elevated metallothionein levels.

title: In vitro platinum drug chemosensitivity of human cervical squamous cell carcinoma cell lines with intrinsic and acquired resistance to cisplatin.

evidence_summary: PRL stimulation promoted proliferation in ovarian and endometrial cancer cell lines; chronic PRL exposure induced malignant transformation of normal ovarian epithelial cells (clonogenicity, soft agar growth, tumor formation in SCID mice), and Ras inhibitor blocked transformation, validating PRL and Ras pathway oncogenic roles.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: PRL induced proliferation in ovarian and endometrial cancer cell lines; chronic exposure transformed normal ovarian epithelial cells to clonogenic, anchorage-independent growth and tumor formation in SCID mice; transformation blocked by Ras inhibitor.
validated_targets.specific_model_name: ovarian and endometrial cancer cell lines, human immortalized normal ovarian epithelial cells, SCID-beige mice

validated_targets.experimental_detail: PRL activated Ras oncogene; Ras inhibitor diminished PRL-induced malignant transformation of normal ovarian epithelial cells, confirming Ras pathway mediates PRL oncogenic effect.

title: Biological significance of prolactin in gynecologic cancers.

evidence_summary: RNAi-mediated LRIG1 knockdown attenuated Smac mimetic SM-164 growth inhibition and TNFα expression in breast and ovarian cancer cells; multitargeted RTK inhibitors crizotinib and GSK1363089 enhanced SM-164 activity in resistant cells and suppressed tumor outgrowth in vivo.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: LRIG1 downregulation by RNAi attenuated SM-164-induced growth inhibition and TNFα expression, and increased RTK activity including c-Met and Ron.
Inhibition of RTKs by crizotinib and GSK1363089 enhanced SM-164 anticancer activity in resistant cell derivatives and completely inhibited resistant tumor outgrowth in vivo.

title: LRIG1 modulates cancer cell sensitivity to Smac mimetics by regulating TNFα expression and receptor tyrosine kinase signaling.

evidence_summary: Combined treatment with DNMT inhibitor guadecitabine and PARP inhibitor talazoparib in BRCA wild-type and mutant breast and ovarian cancer cell lines synergistically enhanced PARPi efficacy, increased ROS accumulation, and promoted PARP trapping in a cAMP/PKA-dependent manner; in vivo xenograft models showed decreased tumor growth and increased overall survival.
validation_methods: In vivo xenograft tumor growth analysis

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Inhibition of DNMT1 by guadecitabine combined with PARP inhibitor talazoparib synergistically increased ROS accumulation and sensitized breast and ovarian cancer cells to PARPi, and enhanced PARP trapping, leading to reduced xenograft tumor growth and improved survival in BRCA-proficient models.
validated_targets.specific_model_name: Breast and ovarian cancer cell lines (BRCA-wild-type/mutant), mice bearing BRCA-proficient high-grade serous ovarian and triple-negative breast cancer xenografts

validated_targets.experimental_detail: PARP inhibition by talazoparib combined with DNMT inhibitor guadecitabine resulted in enhanced PARP trapping and synergistic cancer cell killing, independent of BRCA mutation status, with decreased tumor growth in BRCA-proficient xenograft models.
validated_targets.specific_model_name: Breast and ovarian cancer cell lines (BRCA-wild-type/mutant), mice bearing BRCA-proficient high-grade serous ovarian and triple-negative breast cancer xenografts

title: An Effective Epigenetic-PARP Inhibitor Combination Therapy for Breast and Ovarian Cancers Independent of BRCA Mutations.

evidence_summary: Ectopic expression and azacytidine-induced reexpression of MLH1 in ovarian (A2780/CP70) and colorectal (RKO) cancer cells, and comparison of isogenic MSH2-proficient/deficient endometrial cancer cells (HEC59), showed that loss of MLH1 or MSH2 leads to shortened G2 arrest and rapid dephosphorylation of cdc2 after ionizing radiation without affecting survival.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: MLH1-deficient A2780/CP70 and RKO cells exhibited reduced and shorter G2 arrest and faster decline of phospho-Tyr15-cdc2 after IR compared to MLH1-proficient counterparts.
hMSH2-deficient HEC59 endometrial cancer cells showed similarly altered G2 arrest and rapid loss of phospho-Tyr15-cdc2 after IR relative to MSH2-proficient cells.

title: Loss of DNA mismatch repair imparts defective cdc2 signaling and G(2) arrest responses without altering survival after ionizing radiation.

evidence_summary: Cisplatin/carboplatin-treated cervical and ovarian cancer cell lines induced M2 macrophage polarization via IL-6 and PGE2; tocilizumab (anti-IL-6R), indomethacin (COX inhibitor) and NF-κB blockade each prevented this M2 differentiation, demonstrating target roles in chemoresistance-related immunomodulation.

Indomethacin (COX inhibitor) blocked PGE2 production and prevented M2 macrophage differentiation after chemotherapy.
Blockade of canonical NF-κB signaling abrogated chemotherapy-induced PGE2 and IL-6 production and subsequent M2 differentiation.

title: Chemotherapy alters monocyte differentiation to favor generation of cancer-supporting M2 macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.

evidence_summary: DES-treated Brca1 heterozygous mice showed inhibited mammary branching and ovarian atrophy; Brca2 heterozygous mice exhibited subtle inhibited branching enhanced by DES, demonstrating gene-environment interaction in mammary and ovarian morphology.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: DES-treated BALB/cJ Brca1+/- mice showed inhibited mammary duct branching and atrophied ovaries compared to wild-type littermates, indicating modulation of estrogenic response by Brca1 mutation.

Untreated 129/SvEv Brca2+/- mice had subtle inhibited mammary branching phenotype enhanced by DES treatment, with no significant ovarian pathology difference from wild-type, demonstrating Brca2 mutation alters mammary response to estrogen.

title: Mice heterozygous for a Brca1 or Brca2 mutation display distinct mammary gland and ovarian phenotypes in response to diethylstilbestrol.

evidence_summary: BLU-222 treatment in ovarian and breast cancer cell lines inhibited proliferation and induced G1 and G2 cell-cycle arrest; functional experiments demonstrated that P16INK4A and CDK4/6 activity are key mediators of BLU-222 sensitivity, and the RB tumor suppressor mediates the antiproliferative response.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Selective inhibition with BLU-222 leads to robust antiproliferation and cell-cycle arrest in ovarian and breast cancer models.
High P16INK4A expression characterizes CDK2-inhibition-sensitive models; functional studies demonstrate P16INK4A is a key mediator of BLU-222 sensitivity.
Functional studies confirm CDK4/6 activity is a critical mediator of BLU-222 sensitivity in cancer cell lines.
The RB tumor suppressor mediates the strength of antiproliferative response and the G1-S versus G2-M accumulation profile induced by BLU-222.

title: Tumor Suppressors Condition Differential Responses to the Selective CDK2 Inhibitor BLU-222.
